title: the Kuiper Line Rising Revisited
premise: Wendell Marchetti, the last xenolinguist on Meridian Station, has spent years documenting a colony being quietly abandoned by its parent corporation, dreaming now only in the alien trade-tongue they once studied. When an audit reveals Wendell's name on the manifest of the Kuiper Line—a ship that never flew, supposedly lost with all hands—they realize someone is rewriting history to make them a martyr, or a scapegoat. Racing to the relay at the edge of dead space before the jump window closes, Wendell must decide whether to expose the colony's death or preserve the fiction that lets the survivors vanish and start over. In the end, Wendell sends both signals: the truth into the archive, and silence to the company, choosing belonging with the forgotten over survival as their instrument.
about_author: Oscar Kavanagh is a former radio astronomer who left observatory work to write about the people who stay behind when institutions move on. They live in a coastal town where the fog arrives on schedule, like a signal from something patient.

chapters.title: The Language of Empty Rooms
chapters.summary: Wendell records the final evacuation of Habitat Four, noting how the departing colonists' speech loses inflection as hope drains out. Alone among empty quarters, they dream again in the trade-tongue. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: quiet grief disguised as professional detachment—the loneliness of being the one who stays.

chapters.title: Manifest Errors
chapters.summary: A routine supply audit flags an anomaly: Wendell Marchetti, listed as crew on the Kuiper Line, a colony ship recorded as lost forty years ago. Their own handwriting appears on the scanned manifest. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: uncanny dread—someone knows them intimately, or wants the universe to believe they died.

chapters.title: What the Company Owes the Dead
chapters.summary: Wendell confronts Administrator Voss, who deflects with bureaucratic warmth but privately warns them to stop asking questions. A second name on the false manifest belongs to a child who never existed. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: rising paranoia; the colony's death was not neglect but design.

chapters.title: The Archivist of Meridian
chapters.summary: Wendell seeks out Ilsa Reyes, a half-forgotten data archivist living in the station's sealed lower decks, who confirms the manifest was inserted recently—by someone with corporate root access. POV: alternating Wendell and Ilsa. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance; two invisible people recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Dreams in Trade-Tongue
chapters.summary: Sleep-deprived, Wendell deciphers fragments of the old alien grammar embedded in the forged manifest itself—a message hidden for anyone fluent enough to read it. It names coordinates at the relay. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: wonder rekindled; the dead language is speaking, and it knows things.

chapters.title: Voss Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: The administrator offers Wendell passage off-station and a clean identity if they sign off on the colony's closure report—becoming officially dead, officially complicit. Wendell refuses. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: moral crossroads; the price of survival made explicit and refused.

chapters.title: Dead Space Window
chapters.summary: Ilsa reveals the jump window through dead space opens in six days and won't recur for a year. They steal a maintenance skiff while Voss locks down the docks. POV: alternating, tension split between pilot and stowaway stations. Emotional beat: desperate momentum; no way back now.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: At the ancient relay, Wendell finds evidence others were here before—colonists who 'died' on paper and chose exile instead. The hidden message was theirs: an invitation, not a trap. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: awe and vertigo; the forgotten built their own country.

chapters.title: Signal Race
chapters.summary: As the jump window closes, Voss's pursuit ship arrives demanding Wendell's surrender and the archive drives. Wendell transmits the colony's true record into the open network—irreversible—then cuts the relay's corporate uplink. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: climax; truth released, consequences accepted.

chapters.title: Kuiper Line Rising
chapters.summary: Through the closing window, Wendell and Ilsa follow the exiles' beacon to a settlement beyond company reach. Wendell finally dreams in two languages at once. The archive lives; the survivors belong to themselves. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution—survival achieved by refusing its terms.
